create.name: Chinmaya Mission
create.bio:
Chinmaya Mission is an Advaita Vedanta organisation started in India in 1953 by Swami Chinmayananda, a disciple of Swami Tapovan Maharaj in the Himalayas. His aim was to take the teaching of the Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita out of the forest ashram and into ordinary city life, in plain language and with an emphasis on practice. After his death in 1993 the work passed to Swami Tejomayananda, and today Swami Swaroopananda guides it as global head. Its governing trust is based in Mumbai, and it runs more than 350 centres around the world.

The mission teaches through public lecture series known as jnana yajnas, weekly study groups, residential camps and ashram stays, and a free live-in Vedanta course in the gurukula style that has trained its teachers since 1963. There are classes for children and young adults, devotional singing and chanting, and distance-learning courses in Vedanta and Sanskrit. Its YouTube channel, running since 2009, carries English talk series on the Gita by Swami Swaroopananda, chanting and japa led by Swami Tejomayananda, archive footage of the founder and short clips, with some material in Hindi.

courses.title: Residential Vedanta Course
courses.description: A live-in gurukula course for committed students, centred on the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gita and the Brahma Sutras, with Sanskrit, Vedic chanting and devotional texts. The mission provides board, lodging and books at no charge.

courses.title: Chinmaya Spiritual Camps
courses.description: Short live-in retreats at the mission's ashrams and centres for individuals, families and children, combining Vedanta classes, devotional practice and reflection. Individual stays at an ashram can also be arranged.

courses.title: Postal and eVedanta Courses
courses.description: Home-study lessons in Vedanta first designed by Swami Chinmayananda, now offered online as well, covering the Gita, the Upanishads, Sanskrit and related subjects. The full course list is held by the Chinmaya International Foundation.

free_resources.title: Study Groups and Devi Groups
free_resources.description: Small local circles of five to fifteen people who meet regularly to read a Vedanta text together, discuss it and chant. Devi Groups are the women's version.

free_resources.title: Chinmaya Mission Articles
free_resources.description: Short pieces on applying Vedanta to everyday life, from the mission's resources section.

free_resources.title: Chinmaya Mission Downloadables
free_resources.description: Free downloadable material from the mission, gathered on one page of its resources section.
